newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech, Sprint both post higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech, Sprint both post higher profits.

text.p: Ameritech Corp. and Sprint Corp., two of the nation's prominent communications companies, said Tuesday they posted profit increases in the third quarter.
Ameritech, which is based in Chicago, said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 edged up to $519 million, or 94 cents a share, from $512 million, or 92 cents a share.

The company, which provides local phone service in the Midwest and also operates in all 50 states and 40 countries, said revenues rose 10 percent to $3.7 billion from $3.4 billion as it core communications business generated solid growth.
Sprint, the global communications company based in Kansas City, Mo., said its net income rose 16 percent to $312.4 million, or 72 cents a share, from $268.5 million, or 76 cents a share.
The difference in the per-share figures are a reflection of far more shares outstanding this year than last year -- 434.7 million vs. 350.5 million.
Sprint, which provides long-distance, local and wireless communications services, said its revenues grew to $3.54 billion from $3.21 billion.
For the year to date, Sprint said, net income grew 27 percent to $938.5 million, or $2.22 a share, from $739 million, or $2.10 a share. Revenues expanded to $10.42 billion from $9.42 billion.
The company said international investments drove more than one-third of its earnings growth in the quarter, led by investments in Belgacom of Belgium, Matav of Hungary and Telecom New Zealand.

Ameritech said its nine-month net income slipped 1.9 percent to $1.56 billion, or $2.83 a share, from $1.60 billion, $2.88 a share, despite a 12 percent growth in revenues to $11.0 billion from $9.9 billion.
Ameritech's stock lost $1 to $54.25 while Sprint added 50 cents to $40.375 in early afternoon trading, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
